maudhui: (1) Without prejudice to the provisions of any law enacted by Parliament, the powers of the President as Commander-in-Chief shall include the power to order the armed forces of the country to engage in military operations connected with the defence of the United Republic, the rescue of life and property in times of emergency and other matters which the Commander-in-Chief considers necessary, and for this purpose the Commander-in-Chief may order the armed forces to engage in such operations within or outside Tanzania. (2) Without prejudice to the provisions of a law enacted by Parliament, the Commander-in-Chief shall have power over the following matters— (a) the appointment of top commanders in the armed forces of the United Republic; (b) the appointment of persons to join the armed forces and the discharge of members of the armed forces; (c) the appointment of members of the armed forces to command various units of the armed forces; and (d) the power to order any member of the armed forces not to exercise any power vested in that member by virtue of his being a member of the armed forces. (3) Anything done by any member of the armed forces in contravention of an order issued by the Commander-in-Chief pursuant to the provisions of subarticles (1) and (2) of this Article shall be void.
